layers.note: A tall perennial herb of the herb layer.

moisture.note: Colonises open, disturbed ground across most moisture levels; scarce on waterlogged soil.

heat_load.note: Grows on every aspect in the open.

max_slope_deg.note: Colonises slides and steep, raw slopes.

shade_tolerance.note: Very intolerant of shade: abundant after fire or clearing and fading as the canopy closes.

coldest_c.note: Very cold winters borne: coldest-month means from about −25 °C (gone by −35 °C), as across the boreal forest.

hard_freeze_c.note: Among the hardiest: lows to about −50 °C borne.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 8 to 24 °C; gone below 5 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: Across its range, about 600 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 300.

degree_days_5.note: Across its range, about 200 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 50.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No limit in its range: summer-dry coasts to continental summer rain.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in western Washington lowland forests; not yet checked against Silvics of North America (Burns and Honkala, 1990) or the Fire Effects Information System, both public-domain USDA Forest Service works. Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Fireweed is circumboreal, from lowland clearings to above the tree line (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
